Amenti-Technical-Briefs/main/BRIEF-WHAT-.what: WHAT A SOURCE MUST BE, 1 Sep 2026. THE CITATION POLICY, written because seventy-two briefs existed and none of them was this one — the machinery had run for days while the reasoning lived scattered across a workflow header, a probe comment and a log. A source is an instruction for FINDING THE SAME WORDS AGAIN, not a gesture at provenance. Four grades and not two, because a boolean would have called the work finished and hidden the translations: CITED (an edition reachable again), DATED, THIN (a translator named and no edition — and for a translated text THE EDITION IS HALF THE CITATION, since a famous line can exist in one English text and not another), EMPTY. LINKED is not a fault; a url IS a citation. EMPTY alone fails the build, because a permanently red build is a build nobody reads. Records the probe's own two corrections and the doctrine they share: A RULE THAT FLAGS CORRECT WORK TEACHES THE READER TO IGNORE THE REPORT. §7 carries the policy into the hall and names the largest open gap — the hall may quote only from the text it was handed, and nothing tests that it did.

Amenti-Technical-Briefs/main/BRIEF-THE-D.section: the briefs — 41 files, 8 of them linked anywhere
Amenti-Technical-Briefs/main/BRIEF-THE-D.what: THE DESCRIPTION STAYS WHERE THE TRUTH WAS, 1 Sep 2026. A FAULT WITH NO ERROR MESSAGE, five instances in two sessions and none of them searched for. A thing is built, someone writes down what it is, the writing is TRUE — then the ship moves and the description stays. It does not decay; it stays confident and becomes false, and nothing throws. THE FIVE: Page2's gloss saying 'microphone' while the file held a double helix; probe3 testing a voice engine that had been extracted into the bundle; Page1's BROWSE tab still keyed `data-page="timeline"` while holding a roster browser; the flagship's nav living only in its own markup, so the hall sent a visitor to another repo instead of the tab beside them; and — the register indicting itself — a section NAMED 'the briefs — 41 files' that holds 75, printed into every door list the hall sends. THE DIAGNOSIS: SOURCES.json knows REACHABLE and knows DESCRIBED. It has no way to know whether a description is still true, so `described: true` is forever, and a gloss that is present and false is more dangerous than one that is missing — a missing description makes a reader look, a wrong one makes them act. THE ANSWER IS NOT DISCIPLINE: compare a file's git age to its gloss's git age (that alone catches four of the five); derive every fact that can be derived, because a derived description cannot rot; and where a description must be authored, name what it was written FROM and what it was not. Extends to instruments — a test written against an implementation breaks when the implementation moves; one written against the INTENT survives. And its last argument: BUILD THINGS THAT READ THE REGISTERS OUT LOUD. They will embarrass the registers, which is the point.

Amenti.live/main/SKY.csv.section: the registers — read at the hour of writing
Amenti.live/main/SKY.csv.what: THE SKY, COMPUTED. 1,395 rows, 2894 BC to AD 2026, calculated 1 Sep 2026 from JPL's DE422 ephemeris at the Great Pyramid (29.9792N, 31.1342E). Columns: year, body, kind, description. UNLIKE EVENTS.csv THIS IS NOT AUTHORED — no one wrote these down; they were computed, and they can be recomputed and checked. That is the distinction the `kind` column exists to preserve. 1,342 DUE-EAST CROSSINGS: Jupiter 830, Saturn 335, Uranus 117, Neptune 60. A planet rises due east only when its declination is zero, which happens twice per orbit — rare, exact, datable, and meaningful HERE because the Great Pyramid is aligned to true north within arcminutes, so the monument itself defines the line. VERIFIED AGAINST ORBITAL THEORY: 830 against 831 expected, 335 against 334, 117 and 60 exact. The first run was 16% to 161% high and the error GREW with orbital period — the signature of a slow planet sitting near zero declination while annual aberration wobble was counted as repeated crossings. Fixed geocentrically, merging anything closer than half an orbit. 53 ECLIPSE ROWS, AND THEY ARE THE WEAK PART — READ THIS BEFORE USING THEM. Total and annular solar eclipses computed as central over Giza. The DATES are sound. THE PLACES ARE NOT, before roughly AD 1500. ΔT — the gap between clock time and the Earth's actual rotation — is 5.8 hours at 763 BC and nearly 17 at 2500 BC, so the shadow lands THOUSANDS OF KILOMETRES from where a naive calculation puts it; and ΔT that far back is itself reconstructed FROM recorded eclipses. 49 of the 53 are pre-1500. Not one famous recorded eclipse — Nineveh 763 BC, Thales 585 BC — falls central over any of eight tested sites. RECOMMENDED: strip them, and let eclipses be AUTHORED history in EVENTS.csv where the chronicler is the source, since the record is better evidence than the reconstruction and is the reconstruction's own source. THE ALIGNMENTS ARE UNAFFECTED: declination does not care about ΔT, which shifts the time of day and not the year. DENSITY, for whatever draws it: in a 200-year window, Neptune 2, eclipses 2, Uranus 4, Saturn 14, Jupiter 34. At one crossing every six years JUPITER IS A METRONOME, NOT A MARKER — tier by rarity or the axis carries 64 marks and reads as noise. AND A NULL RESULT WORTH KEEPING: Jupiter–Saturn great conjunctions were tested against the roster on 31 Aug and landed on exactly as many souls as randomly chosen years — 33 of 143 against 32 expected. Show cycles as anchors; never let a surface imply they mean anything.
Amenti.live/main/SKY.csv.authority: COMPUTED, not authored. Recomputable from DE422. The 53 eclipse rows are provisional — see above.

Amenti.live/main/EVENTS.csv.section: the registers — read at the hour of writing
Amenti.live/main/EVENTS.csv.what: THE HISTORICAL ANCHORS. 488 events, 9500 BC to 2024, in sixteen categories — Göbekli Tepe, cuneiform, Hammurabi, Marathon, the Hijra, Hastings, Constantinople, the Principia. Columns: year, name, category, description. LIFTED OUT OF Page2.html ON 1 SEP 2026, where they had been hardcoded and readable by exactly one surface; Page2 now fetches this file via AMENTI_CONFIG.EVENTS_CSV_URL and its inline seed is gone. A RELATIVE PATH ON PURPOSE — same-origin from Pages, so no CORS, no share setting that can change unnoticed, and a register the walk can see. WHAT IT IS FOR: anchors, not claims. It places a reader in time beside the roster's lifespans — at −480 a chart shows Leonidas dying AND Thermopylae. Seventeen of thirty-five test landmarks need no entry here at all, because the soul who died in them is already dated in ROSTER-INDEX.json; this file supplies what deaths cannot, a battle won or a book published. THERE IS NO LONGER A FALLBACK: if this file cannot be fetched the beta helix is EMPTY, and Page2 says so loudly rather than quietly using a seed. A probe should assert the COUNT and not merely presence — an empty fetch is caught, but a TRUNCATED one parses partial and replaces nothing (209 rows survived a mid-file cut in testing). THE STANDING SLIP #44.
Amenti.live/main/EVENTS.csv.authority: AUTHORED, and thin on the Roman Republic and on everything before Solomon — see SLIP #44.

Amenti.live/main/LIBRARY.json.section: the registers — read at the hour of writing
Amenti.live/main/LIBRARY.json.what: THE LIBRARY, READ. What reading rooms exist and which actually hold works — 52 rooms, 550 works, 31 MB of text, every one with its title, its section and ITS SOURCE. THIS IS THE CORPUS, and it was here all along: most works carry a full citation with translator, edition and Project Gutenberg number. Josephus has all 29 books; Shakespeare 45 works and the First Folio; Caesar both commentaries in McDevitte 1869. A room's `missing` array names manifest entries whose files are absent, and hasCard/hasTerminal say whether the room is wired to the rest of the site.
Amenti.live/main/LIBRARY.json.authority: LIVE, and GENERATED by probes/probe-library.mjs — never hand-edited. Meaning and citations live in the per-figure manifests at library/{key}.json. THE READING IS ONLY AS HONEST AS THOSE MANIFESTS: on 29 Aug it faithfully reported 77 blank sources in the Lincoln room, which were not a mystery but one book's table of contents — Speeches and Letters of Abraham Lincoln 1832-1865, ed. Merwin Roe, PG #14721 — with the citation written once on the single work pulled into its own file and never propagated. Fixed with tools/cite.js. AN EMPTY SOURCE STRING READS AS A FIELD RATHER THAN A GAP, which is why it sat unnoticed on the most-quoted figure on the site.

Amenti.live/main/probes/probe-citations..what: THE CITATION AUDIT. Reads LIBRARY.json and grades every work's source into four states — CITED (an edition that can be found again), DATED (a year, no identifier), THIN (a name with nothing to find it by), EMPTY — plus LINKED, which is not a fault. Says WHICH thing each room needs rather than only that something is wrong. First run, 29 Aug 2026: 405 cited, 77 empty, 52 thin — 11 rooms of 52.
Amenti.live/main/probes/probe-citations..authority: LIVE. Exists because probe-library.mjs faithfully RECORDS what the manifests say and nothing READ what it recorded: 77 blank sources sat in the Lincoln room, on the most-quoted figure on the site, for as long as they were blank. AN EMPTY SOURCE STRING READS AS A FIELD RATHER THAN A GAP. EMPTY fails the run; THIN and DATED report and do not, so a gap somebody is working through cannot hold a workflow red for weeks. It is careful about what it refuses to call a fault — a link-out, a pointer to another shelf on this site, and the project's own published work are all correct citations, and its first draft flagged the last of those until it was taught otherwise. A RULE THAT FLAGS CORRECT WORK TEACHES THE READER TO IGNORE THE REPORT.

Amenti.live/main/CITATIONS.json.section: the registers — read at the hour of writing
Amenti.live/main/CITATIONS.json.what: THE CITATION READING. Every reading room graded on whether its works can be traced back to a findable edition, and a plain sentence per room saying what it still needs. The answer to 'can this quotation be checked?' for 550 works at once.
Amenti.live/main/CITATIONS.json.authority: LIVE. Written by probes/probe-citations.mjs from LIBRARY.json. It records the timestamp of the reading it audited, so an audit of a stale library says so rather than passing for current.

Amenti.live/main/SERVES.semantics.json.section: the registers — read at the hour of writing
Amenti.live/main/SERVES.semantics.json.what: WHAT ALREADY SERVES THIS. The register keyed by the QUESTION A BUILDER ASKS rather than by the file that answers it — 22 needs, each with what serves it, WHAT IT DOES NOT ANSWER, and a note. Opened 29 Aug 2026 after the same fault twice in one session: a corpus written while LIBRARY.json held 550 works, and a reader's manual written when an operator's map had been asked for. Every other register in this fleet is keyed by PATH, so learning whether a capability exists means reading 181 glosses and recognising one. Nobody does that, and things get built twice.
Amenti.live/main/SERVES.semantics.json.authority: AUTHORED BY HAND, and READ AT THE TOP OF A BUILD. Its law: A CAPABILITY THAT IS NOT IN THIS FILE WILL BE BUILT AGAIN — not a threat, a description of what happened. `doesNotAnswer` is as load-bearing as `servedBy`: a register that says what it covers and not what it omits invites the second mistake, trusting it too far. Needs with servedBy null are the honest state, not a gap — a need written down and unbuilt is a need that will not be built twice.

Amenti.live/main/probes/probe-serves.mjs.what: Checks every file named in SERVES.semantics.json against SOURCES.json and writes SERVES.json. Five states: SERVED, PARTIAL (built and not wired), UNSERVED (nothing built, and it says so), BROKEN (points at nothing), UNWALKED (real, and outside what the index covers).
Amenti.live/main/probes/probe-serves.mjs.authority: LIVE. Its reason: AN ENTRY POINTING AT A FILE THAT IS NOT THERE IS WORSE THAN NO ENTRY — a builder sent down a dead path by a confident document. Its first run called amenti-doctrine.js and amenti-visits.js BROKEN; both exist, and the finding was that SOURCES.json WALKS ONLY .md AND .json AT THE ROOT, so the entire engine is invisible to the index. That became the UNWALKED state. IT CANNOT FIND A NEED NOBODY HAS WRITTEN DOWN, and says so: a walk verifies a named file exists and cannot invent the question it answers.

Amenti.live/main/.github/workflows/citat.what: THE CITATIONS WATCH. Reads the library and grades every source — on every change to library/, on a :47 rung, and by hand. Fires on CHANGE rather than only on a clock, because the moment to ask where a text came from is while whoever added it still remembers. EMPTY fails the run; THIN and DATED report and do not, so a room whose translator is named and whose edition is not yet found is mid-work rather than broken.
Amenti.live/main/.github/workflows/citat.authority: LIVE. NO continue-on-error ANYWHERE, deliberately: on 24 Aug 2026 merge.js threw under it and the manifest froze for ninety hours behind a green tick. Its audit step tells a CRASH apart from a FINDING — exit 2 means the instrument did not run and says NOTHING BELOW IS A READING, exit 1 means a work has no source. The first draft used `|| echo empty=1`, which is the same blindness written small: it would have reported a missing LIBRARY.json as an empty citation. The readings are committed BEFORE the gate, so a red run still leaves a register behind.

Amenti.live/main/.github/workflows/cite-.what: CITE A ROOM. Run from the Actions tab: give a room key and a citation, and it stamps every work in that room that has none, regenerates LIBRARY.json and CITATIONS.json, and commits. DRY RUN IS ON BY DEFAULT — the first run shows exactly what would change and writes nothing. With the source left blank it reports the gap and stops, which is the correct first run.
Amenti.live/main/.github/workflows/cite-.authority: LIVE. IT EXISTS BECAUSE tools/cite.js WAS BUILT AS A COMMAND FOR A CAPTAIN WHO WORKS FROM GITHUB IN A BROWSER AND HAS NO TERMINAL TO TYPE IT INTO. A tool that cannot be reached by the person who needs it is not a tool; it is a file. Shares the `citations` concurrency lane with the citations watch so the two can never write LIBRARY.json over each other. Other rooms still holding empty sources do NOT fail this run — it stamped the room it was asked to stamp — but a crashed audit does.

Amenti.live/main/slip/SLIP-ADDENDUM-THE-.what: THE EDITIONS STILL TO FIND, opened 30 Aug 2026. THE CITATION WORK IS DONE and this holds what is left of it: nine rooms that name a translator and stop short of the edition that would let a reader find the text again. 550 works, 495 cited, EMPTY zero — against 482 and 77 blanks the same morning. Carries the method that identified Lincoln’s and Hume’s editions (match the room’s titles, in their order, against a book’s table of contents), the whole cite-a-room procedure in three modes, and the three form-field traps met live.
